messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a ~30% token/sec drop on canary after the scheduler prefetch tuning change (PR #4821). Spikes in queueing_time in the continuous-batcher traces. Graph: https://redwood.internal/g/plots/rollout/4821

samir: Which rollout id? can you paste a single trace and the exact repro command?

maya: rollout id `rollout-20260315-42` (canary). repro: `./bench --target=canary --workload=chatty --rps=1500 --seq=128`
Attached a flame sample from the trace (small):
```
continuous_batcher::queueing_time  62ms
continuous_batcher::drain_time     8ms
kernel_selector::memcopy_calls     12
kernel_selector::fallbacks        7
kv_cache::lookup_latency          1.2ms
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `rollout-20260315-42` for service=runtime-scheduler progressed to 50% at 10:14 UTC (sha=6f8a3d).

olivia: Ran a quick microbench on my laptop against the canary patch — I reproduced the dip locally when `batch_target_ms` was lowered. With old settings: `tokens/s=9800`, new: `tokens/s=6800`. Looks like under-sizing batches for short seq workloads.

li: Hmm — that memcopy/fallback count is worrying. PR #4821 touches the prefetch map keys; if KV cache keys change coherence could be worse so we're missing prefix hits and causing more small batches. Can someone bisect the exact commit?

jordan: did a quick git-bisect across the canary history, culprit looks like commit `f3b2c7a` from PR #4821 (changed prefetch key derivation). Patch that reverts key normalization restores hits and tokens/s on my canary test.

maya: Can we hold the rest of the rollout? This is a user-facing throughput regression. Requesting rollback of `rollout-20260315-42`. cc @deploy-bot / @ops-bot :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Rollout hold created for `rollout-20260315-42` by maya. Notifying infra oncall and pausing further promotion.

samir: OK — assign to eng-runtime for revert PR. li, jordan please prepare minimal revert for the key derivation and add a unit test exercising KV hit-rate for short prefixes.

li: Will open revert PR and add deterministic kv-hit integ test. Also adding perf regression CI check for tokens/s drop >10% on canary workloads.

maya: Thanks — leaving traces and benchmark artifacts in the thread: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/4821-canary-traces.zip

jordan: follow-up: adding a quick profiling snippet to the PR description to show where the queueing time accumulates. That should make review faster.

olivia: After revert locally, tokens/s returned to baseline. +1 to shipping the revert and backfilling the regression test. :white_check_mark:
